speaker: jasonseth
text: Okay, proclamation. Whereas the Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs, GEAR UP, is a federally funded program designed to increase the number of students who stay in school and succeed in post-secondary education. And whereas GEAR UP focuses on students from low income and underserved communities who might be the first person in their family to go to college. And whereas GEAR UP provides six or seven year grants to states or partnerships to deliver support and resources to students and their families starting no later than the seventh grade through high school and onward to attaining a post-secondary education. And whereas GEAR UP includes interventions such as tutoring, mentoring, academic preparation and financial education to improve access and success in higher education. And whereas GEAR UP Achievers serves approximately 4,500 students in eighth and ninth grade in four different South King County districts with 2,058 students served from Renton School District. And whereas GEAR UP provides full circle programming including family and community members to support student success and goals by hosting college knowledge workshops, financial aid counseling and family college tours. And whereas the City of Renton is committed to providing a quality education for all students and helping them to achieve their highest potential. Now, therefore I Armando Pavoni, Mayor of the City of Renton do hereby proclaim September 20th through 24th, 2021 to be GEAR UP Week in the City of Renton. And I encourage all citizens to join me in this special observance. And witness whereof I've here to set my hand and cause the seal of the City of Renton to be affixed this 20th day of September, 2021 signed Armando Pavoni, Mayor of the City of Renton.

speaker: kirstenthornton

text: Yeah, I'm here. Hi, first and foremost, thank you, Mayor and Council Members for declaring this to be a peer briefing, just really as a resident of Renton supporting our program. I'm joined here by Christina Park. She is one of our Building Coordinators and Action Services students at Lindbergh High School. And I'm also here with Kevin Smith, who I think is identified as Renton's staff. And he is our Director of Career and Technical Education and oversees our peer program. I will say I made a slight mistake on that proclamation in that we do not service eighth and ninth grade students anymore. We are officially, we have moved into the high schools. We are with ninth and 10th graders. And as you guys all know, last year was extremely chaotic, but one of the best year program years that we've had thus far, servicing close to 1,900 students unduplicated in a variety of services, almost 220 staff across the district in social-emotional learning and supporting students in that. Different PD regarding added implementation, our project-based learning strategies for best practices in the classroom. And then we've also served, we had the opportunity to actually work with over 2,000 families virtually on access to understanding financial aid, college knowledge through our different workshops that we've provided virtually for our families in partnership with CTE Career Centers. And what we're, I think, most excited about this year as we transition back into in-person work is we are combining forces with CTE's Career Center specialists, and we are redefining our program as the Career and College Success Team. And what we're gonna see is just really amazing things, specifically seventh through 12th grade, and hopefully we'll trickle down and provide services down through our K through five system as well. So we're just really thankful. We're excited for gear week. If you get a chance at any point this week, if you wanna support us, please, please, please wear college gear. Take a picture. You can email me at kirstenthortonatrentonschools.us, and I'd love to see you guys supporting our mission, and you'll enter to a raffle to win a prize. And yeah, thank you so much again, and it's truly a pleasure.

speaker: armondopavone
text: Okay, thank you. Next, we'll open the remote audience comment period. It remains the strong intent of the city to have public comment regularly included on our agendas. Each speaker will be given five minutes to speak. You'll be called upon by a city staff member. The staff member will call the speaker's name and unmute the appropriate microphone, which will send an automatic prompt to the speaker of you have been unmuted. This is the speaker's cue that it's their turn to speak. Please begin your comments by stating your name, city of residence, and the topic you're addressing. Speakers should be able to see a timer on the screen. Please finish your comments when you see the time is close to expiring. So we have something new. Residents and others who wish to speak during audience comment period will be required to register in advance. A link to the registration form will be included on future agendas, as well as being posted to the city's council's webpage. The council agenda, portal webpage, and various city social media sites. We are making these changes for three reasons. One, to ensure that everyone who desires to speak during the audience comment portion of the meeting is recognized and afforded the opportunity. Two, to allow city staff the ability to collect speakers' email addresses and phone numbers so we can provide a more immediate response to the residents' concerns. And three, establish a more formal process for records management. Okay, and with that, you know, as we all know, with COVID and everything being remote, this has been a learning process. It's not easy to have the city council meetings be remote like this. It takes quite a bit of organization. And this is one of those areas that we've been changing along the way and looking for the best possible outcome. And I think this'll be very similar to what in-person meetings will look like. It's the same exact form as in-person meetings. And we will accept signups as late as five o'clock on the night of. So it's not much different than in-person meetings. Today, we did take a look at it and it was a little difficult to find the registration.
